items.description: Fix BarrelList: match built-in list indexing and insertion at either boundary after internal split; ensure empty tail sublists don't break pop()
items.hypothesis: The boundary indexing bug is in `_translate_index`: when `index` equals `len(self)` or an out-of-range positive index, the loop walks past the last sublist without breaking, leaving `rel_idx` >= the last sublist length (or `list_idx == len(self.lists)`), so the subsequent `rel_idx < 0` check does not fire and `__getitem__` accesses an invalid slot (or wraps to a wrong element) instead of raising `IndexError`. The `index < 0` branch also can produce `index == len(self)` when index is very negative, leading to the same wrap behavior.
items.next_action: In `boltons/listutils.py`, fix `_translate_index(self, index)` (around lines 108-119) to explicitly reject out-of-range indices before the loop: after `index += len(self)` for negatives, or for positives, if `index < 0 or index >= len(self): return None, None`. Then verify with a split BarrelList that `bl[len(bl)]`, `bl[len(bl)+1]`, and very negative indices raise `IndexError`, and that valid boundary insertions and `pop()` with empty tail sublists behave like built-in list.
